item.title: Two ways big bets on data centers might affect you (Two Indicators)
item.description:
Your money might be fueling the AI boom … just as some AI data center bets are starting to look riskier. If you own stocks, that money is likely tied up in giant tech companies like Microsoft and Nvidia. And if your 401(k) has money invested in the US bond fund, you might be lending tech companies the money to build data centers. 

Today on the show, two stories from our short daily podcast The Indicator from Planet Money on how risky these data center bets are for investors and the companies making them. And, of course, for all of us. 

Read: 

  • Our book: Planet Money: A Guide to the Economic Forces That Shape Your Life 
  • Our weekly longform Planet Money newsletter
  • Our weekly Indicator round-up newsletter
Follow:

The original Indicator episodes were produced by Corey Bridges and Julia Ritchey. They were engineered by Kwesi Lee and Cena Loffredo, fact checked by Sierra Juarez and edited by Kate Concannon. This episode of Planet Money was produced by Vito Emanuel and Emma Peaslee. Alex Goldmark is our executive producer.

item.title: Why Gold? (Classic)
item.description:
In the past few months, the price of gold has gone way up – even hitting a new high last month at just over $2,400 per troy ounce.

Gold has long had a shiny quality to it, literally and in the marketplace. And we wondered, why is that?

Today on the show, we revisit a Planet Money classic episode: Why Gold? Jacob Goldstein and David Kestenbaum will peruse the periodic table of the elements with one goal in mind: to learn which element would really make the best money.

This classic Planet Money episode was part of the Planet Money Buys Gold series, and was hosted by Jacob Goldstein and David Kestenbaum.

This rerun was hosted by Sally Helm, produced by Willa Rubin, edited by Keith Romer, and fact-checked by Sierra Juarez. Alex Goldmark is our executive producer.
